records.subject: Cab Calloway — St. James Infirmary Blues
Big Bopper — Chantilly Lace
concreteFacts: Chantilly Lace is performed by Big Bopper.
The song peaked at #6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 25 weeks on the chart.
The song was recorded at Gold Star Studios in Houston, Texas.
The original release was as the flip side to "The Purple People Eater Meets The Witch Doctor".
The song was reissued by Mercury Records in the summer of 1958.
The song was the third most played song of 1958.
Jerry Lee Lewis recorded a version of the song in January 1972.

records.subject: Conway Twitty — It's Only Make Believe
Nancy Sinatra — These Boots Are Made For Walking
Tony Joe White — Polk Salad Annie
concreteFacts: Polk Salad Annie is performed by Tony Joe White.
The song appears on the album "Tony Joe White" (1971).
The song peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 12 weeks on the chart.
Tony Joe White's version of 'Polk Salad Annie' was performed with Dave Grohl and the Foo Fighters on Late Show With David Letterman in 2014.
Tony Joe White's childhood in Oak Grove, Louisiana, influenced the song's depiction of Southern rural life.
The song 'Polk Salad Annie' includes spoken word segments and nonsensical noises in the intro and outro.

records.subject: Bee Gees — To Love Somebody
concreteFacts: To Love Somebody is performed by Bee Gees.
The song appears on the album "Their Greatest Hits--The Record" (2001).
The song peaked at #17 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 9 weeks on the chart.
The song was reissued in 1980 on RSO Records with "How Can You Mend a Broken Heart" as its flipside.
The song ranked at number 94 on NME magazine's "100 Best Tracks of the Sixties".

records.subject: Bob Seger — Night Moves
concreteFacts: Night Moves is performed by Bob Seger.
The song appears on the album "Night Moves" (1976).
The song peaked at #4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 21 weeks on the chart.
The song was recorded at Nimbus Nine Studios in Toronto, Ontario.
The song was completed in fewer than ten takes.
The song's backing vocals were performed by Sharon Lee Williams, Rhonda Silver, and Laurel Ward and Tracy Richardson.

records.subject: Aerosmith — Sweet Emotion
concreteFacts: Sweet Emotion is performed by Aerosmith.
The song appears on the album "Live Bootleg" (1978).
The song peaked at #36 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 8 weeks on the chart.
The song features a talk box used by Joe Perry.
The song's intro includes a marimba played by Jay Messina.
The song was included on almost every Aerosmith compilation.

records.subject: Dire Straits — Sultans Of Swing
concreteFacts: Sultans Of Swing is performed by Dire Straits.
The song appears on the album "Money For Nothing" (1988).
The song peaked at #4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.
The song was recorded at Pathway Studios in North London in July 1977.
The song was rerecorded at Basing Street Studios in February 1978 for their debut album.
Dire Straits formed in London in 1977 with Mark Knopfler, David Knopfler, John Illsley, and Pick Withers.

records.subject: Mouth & MacNeal — How Do You Do?
Paul Simon — You Can Call Me Al
concreteFacts: You Can Call Me Al is performed by Paul Simon.
The song appears on the album "Graceland" (1986).
The song peaked at #23 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 29 weeks on the chart.
Pierre Boulez, who was attending the same party, mistakenly referred to Paul as "Al" and to Peggy as "Betty", inspiring Simon to write a song.
Chevy Chase lip-synced Simon's vocals as Simon lip-synced to the backing vocals and brought in various instruments to mime playing when they respectively appear in the song.
The original music video was a performance Simon gave during his Saturday Night Live monologue.

records.subject: Phil Collins — In The Air Tonight
Toto — Africa
concreteFacts: Africa is performed by Toto.
The song appears on the album "Toto IV" (1982).
The song peaked at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 21 weeks on the chart.
The song was written by David Paich and Jeff Porcaro.
The music video was directed by Steve Barron.
The music video reached one billion views on YouTube in June 2024.

records.subject: Talking Heads — Once in a Lifetime
concreteFacts: Once In A Lifetime is performed by Talking Heads.
The song appears on the album "Remain In Light" (1980).
The song peaked at #91 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 4 weeks on the chart.
The song was certified platinum in the UK in 2023.
A live version entered the US Billboard Hot 100 in 1986.
NPR named the song one of the 100 most important American musical works of the 20th century.

records.subject: 4 Non Blondes — What's Up
concreteFacts: What's Up is performed by 4 Non Blondes.
The song peaked at #14 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 26 weeks on the chart.
The song was written and produced by Linda Perry, though David Tickle is credited as the producer.
The music video was nominated for Best Alternative Rock Video at the 1993 MTV Video Music Awards.
The song was re-recorded at The Record Plant in Sausalito after initial dissatisfaction with David Tickle's production.
Linda Perry's version of the song was preferred over David Tickle's by Interscope's co-owner Jimmy Iovine.
The band was signed to Interscope in July 1991.

records.subject: Spin Doctors — Two Princes
concreteFacts: Two Princes is performed by Spin Doctors.
The song appears on the album "Pocket Full Of Kryptonite" (1992).
The song peaked at #7 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 29 weeks on the chart.
Spin Doctors performed a modified version of 'Two Princes' on Sesame Street featuring Elmo, Zoe, and Telly.
Spin Doctors made an appearance on Sesame Street (episode 3450) with a modified version of 'Two Princes'.
Spin Doctors recorded a cover of 'Have You Ever Seen the Rain?' for the film Philadelphia.

records.subject: Biz Markie — Just A Friend
concreteFacts: Just A Friend is performed by Biz Markie.
The song appears on the album "The Biz Never Sleeps" (1989).
The song peaked at #9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 22 weeks on the chart.
Karma, a staff record producer for Cold Chillin' Records, produced the single but never received credit.
In 2021, it was ranked at No. 480 on Rolling Stone's Top 500 Best Songs of All Time.
The music video includes a scene of Biz Markie dressed as Mozart in 18th-century clothing.

records.subject: Los Lonely Boys — Heaven
concreteFacts: Heaven is performed by Los Lonely Boys.
The song appears on the album "Los Lonely Boys" (2004).
The song peaked at #16 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 30 weeks on the chart.
The song was covered by Salvador for their album So Natural.
The song is featured in the 2008 Nintendo DS game Guitar Hero: On Tour.
Bo Bice performed the song on American Idol, leading to a 77% increase in album sales.

records.subject: Nickelback — How You Remind Me
concreteFacts: How You Remind Me is performed by Nickelback.
The song appears on the album "The Best Of Nickelback: Volume 1" (2013).
The song peaked at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 49 weeks on the chart.
The song was included in Consequence's list of 50 Kick-Butt Post-Grunge Songs.
The song was re-released worldwide after its initial release in the United States and Canada.
The song was certified Platinum and sold 4.5 million copies in the United States.

records.subject: Chris Stapleton & Justin Timberlake — Tennessee Whiskey & Drink You Away
concreteFacts: Tennessee Whiskey is performed by Chris Stapleton.
The song appears on the album "Traveller" (2015).
The song peaked at #20 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 6 weeks on the chart.
Stapleton and Justin Timberlake performed "Tennessee Whiskey" at the Country Music Association (CMA) Awards in November 2015.
Chris Stapleton's version of "Tennessee Whiskey" was released as a promotional CD single and never officially released to radio as a single.
The album track Tennessee Whiskey was not released as a radio single.

records.subject: Blanco Brown — The Git Up
concreteFacts: The Git Up is performed by Blanco Brown.
The song peaked at #14 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 20 weeks on the chart.
Blanco Brown released "The Git Up" as his debut single on May 3, 2019.
Blanco Brown's debut single "The Git Up" was released in April 2019.
As of October 2022, "The Git Up" has over 300 million streams on Spotify.
Blanco Brown's "The Git Up" Challenge increased in popularity after the video was released and was featured in over 130,000 videos on TikTok.
Blanco Brown posted a YouTube video with country music artist Lainey Wilson to teach people how to do the dance.

records.subject: Alabama Shakes — Hold On
concreteFacts: Hold On is performed by Alabama Shakes.
The song appears on the album "Boys & Girls" (2012).
The song peaked at #93 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 2 weeks on the chart.
The song was performed live in a studio for the music video.
Rolling Stone named "Hold On" the best song of 2012.
The Village Voice's 40th annual Pazz & Jop poll voted "Hold On" as the 11th best single of 2012.
